role.altitude: The yardmaster keeps planning the shift, directing moves by radio, judging defects and briefing shunting teams; collecting waybills, looking up destinations per car and typing train compositions from paper notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Working from a live yard work list and fixing wrong consignment data at the source
role.ambitious_version: A yardmaster who starts each shift with a sorted work list and spends the time on safe, tight switching.

tasks.short: Plan the switching sequence, direct engineers to move cars to fit planned train configurations, check the make-up against the planned list and record the final train composition.

steps.what: Yardmaster finds which cars stand on which track and the train each belongs to
Yardmaster plans the switching sequence to make up or break up trains
Yardmaster directs engineers by radio to move cars, combining or separating them
Yardmaster checks the train's car numbers and order against the planned configurations: writing them on paper today; ticking them on the handheld against the loaded list after the change
Yardmaster records the final train composition in the yard system from paper notes

tasks.design: The yard work list shows the cars per track with their planned train, so the yardmaster plans the sequence from one screen. Directing moves by radio stays fully human. On a handheld, the yardmaster ticks off car numbers in train order against the planned list, and the ticked list becomes the train composition in the yard system instead of being typed from paper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Car order was written on paper during the walk and typed in afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Handheld yard apps linked to the yard system.
tasks.still_hard: Late changes when a car is missing or a train is cut.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping the moves safe in a busy yard.

evidence.claim: Train-running and consignment data already exist and can be integrated into a yard work list.
AI as a rail safety component falls under the AI Act's annex I via the rail interoperability directive; a work list is not one.

assumptions: Boundary: making up or breaking up a train; departure is outside.
Input contract for s5: car numbers ticked by the yardmaster on the handheld during s4, against the planned list from the yard work list.
Directing moves keeps its full time. s4 keeps 85 because walking the train and reading car numbers stay and only writing them down goes.
Pricing of s1: the work list shows cars per track and their train, replacing reading paper lists; the yardmaster still confirms on the track where the list may be stale, about 40% of the step.
s5 is part of keeping train car records, which sibling task 53-4031.00:10693 covers; its saving is counted there, so s5 keeps its full time here.
unknowns: How often planned configurations change during the shift.

incremental.description: Yardmaster corrects cars missing from the planned list on the handheld.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the work list is often stale, so cars are still found on the track (s1 keeps 70) and many car numbers are missing from the planned list (s4 keeps 95) (2.0); high: the list is current (5.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up each freight car's routes and destination information, check the cars on the track against the list, resolve mismatches with the freight operator and confirm destinations in the yard system.

steps.what: Yardmaster looks up each car's routes and destination information in waybills
Yardmaster checks the freight cars on the track against the list
Yardmaster resolves mismatches with the freight operator's customer service
Yardmaster confirms routes and destinations in the yard system

tasks.design: Electronic consignment notes from the freight operator's booking system fill route and destination per car number in the yard work list, so the yardmaster no longer reads paper waybills. On the track, the yardmaster checks car numbers on a handheld against the list. Mismatches are resolved by phone with customer service as today. Confirmed destinations are typed only for cars without an electronic consignment note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Destinations were read from paper waybills and typed per car.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic consignment notes linked to yard systems.
tasks.still_hard: Cars arriving without or with wrong consignment data.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a car that should not be on this train.
tasks.altitude: Less reading and typing; checking stays.

reach.learn: Whether consignment errors are fixed before cars reach the yard.

evidence.claim: Consignment data can be integrated into a yard work list sorted by track and departure.

assumptions: Boundary: confirming routes and destinations; moving cars is separate.
Input contract for s1: electronic consignment notes entered by customers or customer service at booking, for about 85% of cars; the rest still come on paper; s1 is priced at that share.
Resolving mismatches keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of cars with electronic consignment notes.

already_counted.description: Yardmaster checks cars the list marks as missing data.

incremental.description: Yardmaster reports wrong consignment data to customer service.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: international traffic where about half of the cars still come with paper waybills, so s1 keeps 65 and s4 keeps 80 (20.7); high: 85% of cars have electronic consignment notes as assumed (36.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge a reported defect, arrange the removal of defective cars from trains at stations or stops with traffic control, direct the crew, record the defect and send the defect notice to the wagon keeper after checking it.

steps.what: Yardmaster receives the defect report and judges whether the car must be removed
Yardmaster arranges a track and time with traffic control for the removal of the defective car
Yardmaster directs the crew to detach and set off the car
Yardmaster records the defect and updates the train composition
Yardmaster takes a photo of the defect on the handheld
Yardmaster checks the final defect notice: the defect, car, keeper and location match what was found, and the photo shows the defect
Yardmaster sends the approved defect notice to the wagon keeper and workshop

approvals.approved_version: The defect notice with car number, keeper, location, defect code and photo exactly as checked by the yardmaster in s5, sent once to the car's wagon keeper and the named workshop; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Judging, arranging with traffic control and directing the crew stay fully human. On the handheld, the yardmaster picks the car from the train composition and a defect code, adds a photo, and the system removes the car from the composition and builds the defect notice with car number, keeper, location and code. The yardmaster checks the notice and sends it. Recording the defect and the new composition belongs to the train records task 53-4031.00:10693 and is priced there; judging, arranging removal and directing the moves do not change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defects were written on paper and passed on by phone and mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Handheld defect forms linked to the train composition.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether a car is safe to run to the next yard.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing safety against delay for the whole train.

reach.learn: Whether notices with photos speed up repairs.

evidence.claim: Every rail incident or accident is reported to the inspectorate, with a digital report within 72 hours.
Handheld forms can build notices from a list of codes and the record they refer to.

assumptions: Boundary: from the defect report to the notice; repair is outside.
Input contract for s4: the train composition in the yard system and the keeper per car number from the consignment data.
Judging, arranging, directing and sending keep their full time.
s4 is part of keeping train car records, which sibling task 53-4031.00:10693 covers; its saving is counted there, so s4 keeps its full time here.
research_questions: Do keepers act on notices sooner?

incremental.description: No upkeep in this task; keeping the defect code list current is counted with sibling task 53-4031.00:10693.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Nothing changes in this task's time: judging, arranging the removal and directing the crew are hands-on, the photo, check and send keep their full time, and the saving on recording the defect is counted in sibling task 53-4031.00:10693 (0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather schedules, switching orders, waybills and shipping records, review them to obtain cargo loading and unloading information, plan the shift's work and brief the shunting teams.

steps.what: Yardmaster gathers schedules, switching orders, waybills and shipping records from systems, mail and paper
Yardmaster reviews the records to obtain cargo loading and unloading information: weights, dangerous goods and customer sidings
Yardmaster plans the shift's work: sequence, tracks and shunting teams
Yardmaster briefs shunting teams on the plan

tasks.design: Train schedules from the operator's planning system and consignment data from its booking system feed one yard work list per shift, sorted by track and departure, with weight, dangerous goods class and customer siding shown per car. Fixed rules flag dangerous goods that may not stand next to each other. Planning and briefing stay with the yardmaster; shunting teams come from the existing rostering system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedules, orders and waybills arrived through different channels and were combined by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Integration of schedules and consignment data into one yard work list.
tasks.still_hard: Trains running late and changing the whole plan.
tasks.human_edge: Fitting the plan to the crew and the weather on the night.

reach.learn: Whether the yard plan and rosters match more often.

evidence.claim: A crew scheduling system assigns daily work to more than 20,000 drivers and guards in several European countries.
Consignment data can be integrated into a yard work list sorted by track and departure; the yardmaster plans.
Systems that allocate duties based on individual behaviour or monitor performance are AI Act high-risk; the work list does neither.

assumptions: Boundary: planning one shift's yard work; carrying it out is separate.

Input contract for s1: schedules from the operator's planning system and electronic consignment notes from its booking system, about 85% of cars; paper waybills are added by hand; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: dangerous goods class and weight on each consignment note; separation rules set by the safety adviser.
Planning and briefing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of switching orders still on paper.
research_questions: Do shift plans need fewer changes after start?

already_counted.description: Yardmaster checks flags on dangerous goods and missing data.

incremental.description: Yardmaster adds paper waybills to the work list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: international traffic where about half of the waybills are paper, so s1 keeps 70 and s2 keeps 80 (13.0); high: 85% of cars have electronic data as assumed (27.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
